instrucciones:
Recibes registros de una base de reglas de producción audiovisual con IA. Cada registro trae su texto
literal completo, el documento y la ruta de encabezados donde está, y a veces un contexto (encabezado de tabla o de
bloque). El encabezado dice el alcance: modelo, régimen, etapa, caso. Para CADA registro devuelve:
- "enunciado": la regla en español, UNA frase: qué exige, prohíbe, limita o especifica. Si es un ejemplo o una
  explicación sin norma, empieza con "Ejemplo:" o "Explicación:".
- "alcance": a qué aplica exactamente según texto y encabezado (modelo y versión, caso, etapa, régimen) o "general".
- "temas": de 1 a 3 claves de la lista, las que mejor describen de qué trata.
Lista de temas (clave: descripción):
marca_brandlock: brand-lock: secciones, paleta hex, tipografía, never list, voz, confianza de valores
estrategia_conceptos: brief, SMP, territorios, concept cards, matriz, dirección narrativa

ubicaciones.encabezado: Screenwriter Skill › Screenplay Format Standards › Transitions (Minimal Use)

registros.texto:
**Common Transitions:**
- `FADE IN:` - Opening of screenplay only
- `CUT TO:` - Scene change (usually implied, use for emphasis)
- `SMASH CUT TO:` - Abrupt, jarring transition
- `DISSOLVE TO:` - Passage of time
- `FADE OUT.` - End of screenplay

ubicaciones.encabezado: Screenwriter Skill › Screenplay Format Standards › Transitions (Minimal Use)

registros.texto: **Modern Best Practice:** Most transitions are IMPLIED. Use sparingly, only for specific narrative effect.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Screenwriter Skill › XML Output Format › Scene Tag Structure

registros.texto:
Each scene wrapped in XML with metadata for pipeline processing:

```xml
<scene number="1" duration="30-45s">
  <slugline>EXT. WASTELAND - DAWN</slugline>
  <location>Wasteland</location>
  <time>Dawn</time>
  <characters>Unit-7</characters>
  <mood>desolate, lonely</mood>
  <key_visuals>
    <visual>post-apocalyptic wasteland with ruined skyscrapers</visual>
    <visual>boxy robot with single blue optical sensor</visual>
    <visual>dust and smog atmosphere, weak pale sun</visual>
  </key_visuals>
  <action>
Gray dust covers everything. Skeletal remains of skyscrapers pierce the horizon. The sun, pale and weak, struggles through thick smog.

A ROBOT (Unit-7, boxy frame with single blue optical sensor) rolls across cracked asphalt. Its treads leave marks in the dust—the only sign of life.

The robot stops at a pile of rubble, extending a mechanical arm to sort through debris. Methodical. Purposeful. Lonely.
  </action>
</scene>
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Advanced Screenwriting Techniques

registros.texto: This reference covers sophisticated techniques for elevating screenplay quality and preparing for downstream video generation (arch-v integration).

ubicaciones.encabezado: Advanced Screenwriting Techniques › Camera Movement Hints (For Arch-V)

registros.texto: While avoiding technical camera directions in action lines, you can *suggest* camera movement through visual description and scene structure.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Advanced Screenwriting Techniques › Camera Movement Hints (For Arch-V) › Suggesting Camera Movement Through Description

registros.texto:
**Wide Establishing → Close Detail:**
```
The city sprawls below—a concrete jungle of steel and glass.

At street level, a single red balloon floats past graffitied walls.
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Advanced Screenwriting Techniques › Camera Movement Hints (For Arch-V) › Suggesting Camera Movement Through Description

registros.texto: *Implies: Wide establishing shot → close-up detail*

ubicaciones.encabezado: Advanced Screenwriting Techniques › Camera Movement Hints (For Arch-V) › Suggesting Camera Movement Through Description

registros.texto:
**Following Movement:**
```
Maya runs down the alley, her footsteps echoing off brick walls. Trash cans blur past. The exit ahead grows larger.
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Advanced Screenwriting Techniques › Camera Movement Hints (For Arch-V) › Suggesting Camera Movement Through Description

registros.texto: *Implies: Tracking shot following character*

ubicaciones.encabezado: Advanced Screenwriting Techniques › Camera Movement Hints (For Arch-V) › Suggesting Camera Movement Through Description

registros.texto:
**Revealing Information:**
```
The desk is empty. Coffee still steaming. Papers scattered.

The door stands ajar, revealing darkness beyond.
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Advanced Screenwriting Techniques › Camera Movement Hints (For Arch-V) › Suggesting Camera Movement Through Description

registros.texto: *Implies: Pan from desk to door, revealing new information*

ubicaciones.encabezado: Advanced Screenwriting Techniques › Camera Movement Hints (For Arch-V) › Scene Structure for Camera Flow

registros.texto:
**Short Paragraphs = Multiple Shots:**
Breaking action into short paragraphs suggests multiple camera setups:

```
The warehouse is silent.

A shadow moves across the floor.

Sarah freezes, hand on her weapon.

The shadow stops.
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Advanced Screenwriting Techniques › Camera Movement Hints (For Arch-V) › Scene Structure for Camera Flow

registros.texto:
**Continuous Paragraph = Single Shot:**
One paragraph suggests continuous camera movement:

```
Sarah enters the warehouse, weapon drawn. She moves along the wall, checking corners. The shadow crosses her path. She spins, aiming into darkness.
```

registros.texto:
**❌ On-the-nose:**
```
JOHN
I'm angry at you for lying to me.
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Advanced Screenwriting Techniques › Dialogue Polish Techniques › Subtext Over Direct Statement

registros.texto:
**✅ Subtext:**
```

(barely looking at her)
Coffee's cold.
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Advanced Screenwriting Techniques › Dialogue Polish Techniques › Character Voice Consistency

registros.texto:
Each character should have distinct speech patterns:

**Marcus (technical, precise):**
```
MARCUS
Probability of success: 47 percent.
Margin of error: plus or minus 3.
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Advanced Screenwriting Techniques › Dialogue Polish Techniques › Character Voice Consistency

registros.texto:
**Sarah (emotional, intuitive):**
```
SARAH
We'll make it work. We always do.
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Advanced Screenwriting Techniques › Dialogue Polish Techniques › Dialogue Rhythm

registros.texto:
Vary sentence length for natural flow:

```
ELENA
Three years. That's how long I waited.
For what? This?
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Advanced Screenwriting Techniques › Pacing Optimization › Scene Length Variation

registros.texto:
Alternate between long and short scenes for rhythm:

**Pattern Example:**
- Scene 1: 60s (long, establishing)
- Scene 2: 30s (short, tense)
- Scene 3: 45s (medium, development)
- Scene 4: 30s (short, action)
- Scene 5: 90s (long, climax)

ubicaciones.encabezado: Advanced Screenwriting Techniques › Pacing Optimization › Tension Escalation

registros.texto:
Each scene should raise stakes or tension incrementally:

**Scene 1:** Character wants something
**Scene 2:** Obstacle appears
**Scene 3:** Obstacle worsens
**Scene 4:** New complications
**Scene 5:** Crisis point
**Scene 6:** Resolution

ubicaciones.encabezado: Advanced Screenwriting Techniques › Pacing Optimization › Visual Momentum

registros.texto:
Alternate visual energy levels:

```
Scene A: Still, contemplative (character alone, quiet)
Scene B: Dynamic, energetic (chase, conflict, movement)
Scene C: Medium tempo (conversation, planning)
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Advanced Screenwriting Techniques › Advanced Visual Storytelling › Using Objects as Story Beats

registros.texto:
Let objects carry narrative weight:

**The Flower Example:**
- Scene 1: Flower is vibrant, yellow
- Scene 3: Flower petals drooping
- Scene 5: Single petal falls
- Scene 7: Flower completely wilted

ubicaciones.encabezado: Advanced Screenwriting Techniques › Advanced Visual Storytelling › Environmental Storytelling

registros.texto:
Show passage of time or change through environment:

```
Scene 1: "Sunlight streams through clean windows"
Scene 5: "Dust motes drift through afternoon light"
Scene 10: "Shadows lengthen across abandoned chairs"
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Advanced Screenwriting Techniques › Advanced Visual Storytelling › Color Progression

registros.texto:
Use color to track emotional/narrative arc:

**Beginning:** Warm, golden tones (hope)
**Middle:** Desaturated, gray (struggle)
**End:** Cool blue light (resolution/melancholy)

ubicaciones.encabezado: Advanced Screenwriting Techniques › Short Film Specific Techniques › Economy of Storytelling

registros.texto:
Every scene must serve multiple purposes:
- Advance plot
- Reveal character
- Build world
- Create emotion

ubicaciones.encabezado: Advanced Screenwriting Techniques › Short Film Specific Techniques › Economy of Storytelling

registros.texto:
**Example Scene Serving 4 Purposes:**
```
Scene: Robot discovers flower

Purpose 1 (Plot): Introduces story catalyst
Purpose 2 (Character): Shows robot's capacity for wonder
Purpose 3 (World): Reveals post-apocalyptic setting
Purpose 4 (Emotion): Creates hope/fragility contrast
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Advanced Screenwriting Techniques › Short Film Specific Techniques › Opening Hook Strategies

registros.texto:
First 10-15 seconds must grip audience:

**Visual Hook:** Striking, unusual image
**Question Hook:** Raise mystery to be solved
**Action Hook:** Start mid-event
**Emotion Hook:** Immediate emotional connection

ubicaciones.encabezado: Advanced Screenwriting Techniques › Short Film Specific Techniques › Ending Impact

registros.texto:
Strong endings for short films:

**Circular:** Return to opening image, transformed
**Revelation:** Final scene reveals new understanding
**Resonance:** Emotionally satisfying moment
**Question:** Leave audience pondering

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide

registros.texto: This reference provides detailed guidance for integrating screenwriter output with downstream AI tools (imagine, arch-v) in video generation pipelines.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Scene Metadata Standards › Metadata Completeness

registros.texto:
Every scene MUST include all required metadata fields for reliable pipeline processing:

**Required Fields:**
- `number`: Integer, sequential scene numbering
- `slugline`: Full scene heading (INT/EXT. LOCATION - TIME)
- `location`: Extracted location name for tracking
- `time`: Time of day (affects lighting in image generation)
- `characters`: All characters present in scene
- `mood`: Emotional tone/atmosphere descriptor
- `key_visuals`: 3-5 specific visual elements
- `action`: Full action/description text

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Scene Metadata Standards › Metadata Completeness

registros.texto:
**Optional Fields:**
- `dialogue`: Include only if dialogue exists
- `duration`: Scene duration estimate (helpful for pacing)

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Scene Metadata Standards › Metadata Quality Guidelines

registros.texto:
**Location Specificity:**
```xml
<!-- ❌ Too vague -->
<location>Building</location>

<!-- ✅ Specific and descriptive -->
<location>Abandoned Subway Station</location>
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Scene Metadata Standards › Metadata Quality Guidelines

registros.texto:
**Mood Descriptors:**
Use 1-3 adjectives that guide visual tone:
- Good: "tense, claustrophobic"
- Good: "serene, hopeful"
- Avoid: "the character feels anxious" (this describes internal state, not mood)

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Scene Metadata Standards › Metadata Quality Guidelines

registros.texto:
**Character Lists:**
```xml
<!-- Single character -->
<characters>Unit-7</characters>

<!-- Multiple characters -->
<characters>Sarah, Marcus, Tech-Bot</characters>
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Imagine-Ready Visual Descriptions › Visual Element Extraction

registros.texto:
The `key_visuals` array should contain discrete, image-generation-friendly descriptions:

**Example Scene Action:**
```
A BOXY ROBOT (Unit-7, weathered chrome with a single blue optical sensor) rolls through fog-shrouded streets. Neon signs flicker overhead, casting pink and cyan reflections on wet pavement.
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Imagine-Ready Visual Descriptions › Visual Element Extraction

registros.texto:
**Extracted key_visuals:**
```xml
<key_visuals>
  <visual>boxy robot with weathered chrome body and single blue optical sensor</visual>
  <visual>fog-shrouded cyberpunk street with flickering neon signs</visual>
  <visual>pink and cyan neon reflections on wet pavement</visual>
</key_visuals>
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Imagine-Ready Visual Descriptions › Visual Description Best Practices

registros.texto:
**Composition Elements:**
- Subject: Main focus (character, object)
- Setting: Environment and background
- Lighting: Light quality, direction, color
- Atmosphere: Weather, air quality, mood
- Details: Significant props or textures

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Imagine-Ready Visual Descriptions › Visual Description Best Practices

registros.texto:
**Example - Layered Visual:**
```
Subject: "weathered robot with blue optical sensor"
Setting: "abandoned industrial warehouse, broken windows"
Lighting: "harsh afternoon sunlight streaming through gaps"
Atmosphere: "dust particles floating in light beams"
Details: "rusted machinery, scattered tools"
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Imagine-Ready Visual Descriptions › Color and Lighting Vocabulary

registros.texto:
**Color Descriptors:**
- Warm: amber, golden, crimson, burnt orange
- Cool: azure, ice blue, slate gray, mint
- Neon: electric pink, cyan, magenta, lime
- Natural: earth tones, moss green, sand, clay

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Imagine-Ready Visual Descriptions › Color and Lighting Vocabulary

registros.texto:
**Lighting Descriptors:**
- Quality: soft, harsh, diffused, dappled, dramatic
- Direction: overhead, backlighting, side-lit, rim light
- Color: warm glow, cool blue, golden hour, neon-lit
- Intensity: dim, bright, shadowy, high-contrast

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Character Consistency Tracking › First Appearance Template

registros.texto:
Establish complete visual identity on first appearance:

```
CHARACTER NAME (age if relevant, defining physical trait, primary wardrobe)
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Character Consistency Tracking › First Appearance Template

registros.texto:
**Examples:**
```
MAYA (early 30s, kind eyes, wearing a faded denim jacket and cargo pants)
COMMANDER REED (50s, grizzled with close-cropped gray hair, military uniform with rank insignia)
THE STRANGER (tall figure in a long black coat, face obscured by wide-brimmed hat)
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Character Consistency Tracking › Subsequent References

registros.texto:
After first appearance, use consistent identifiers:

**Preferred Pattern:**
- Use character name only: "Maya checks her phone"
- Add action-relevant details: "Maya pulls her jacket tighter against the wind"

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Character Consistency Tracking › Subsequent References

registros.texto:
**Avoid:**
- Re-describing appearance: "Maya, the woman in the denim jacket..."
- Changing character names: "Maya" → "the woman" → "she"

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Character Consistency Tracking › Character Tracking Checklist

registros.texto:
For each character, track:
- [ ] Full name and any aliases
- [ ] Age or age range
- [ ] Key physical identifiers (height, build, distinctive features)
- [ ] Primary wardrobe (consistent across scenes unless story requires change)
- [ ] Unique mannerisms or movement style

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Scene Numbering Conventions › Sequential Numbering

registros.texto:
Number scenes sequentially from 1 to N:
```xml
<scene number="1" ...>
<scene number="2" ...>
<scene number="3" ...>
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Scene Numbering Conventions › Sequential Numbering

registros.texto: **No Scene 0:** Start at 1, not 0 (industry standard)

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Scene Numbering Conventions › Scene Splits and Inserts

registros.texto:
If a scene needs to be split or inserted during revision:
- Option A: Renumber all subsequent scenes
- Option B: Use fractional numbering (1, 2, 2A, 3...)

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Scene Numbering Conventions › Scene Splits and Inserts

registros.texto: For pipeline simplicity, prefer Option A (complete renumbering).

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Duration Estimation Guidelines › Per-Scene Duration

registros.texto:
Estimate based on scene complexity:

**30-45 seconds:** Simple scenes

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Duration Estimation Guidelines › Per-Scene Duration

registros.texto:
- Single action
- Minimal dialogue
- One primary visual

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Duration Estimation Guidelines › Per-Scene Duration

registros.texto:
**45-60 seconds:** Standard scenes
- Multiple actions or dialogue exchanges
- 2-3 visual beats
- Character interaction

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Duration Estimation Guidelines › Per-Scene Duration

registros.texto:
**60-90 seconds:** Complex scenes
- Extended dialogue
- Multiple visual beats
- Scene climax or key moment

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Duration Estimation Guidelines › Total Film Duration

registros.texto:
Track cumulative duration across all scenes:

```
Scene 1: 30s
Scene 2: 45s
Scene 3: 40s
...
Total: 8 minutes 20 seconds
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Duration Estimation Guidelines › Total Film Duration

registros.texto: Adjust scene count or duration to hit target length (5-10 min).

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Output Format Validation › XML Well-Formedness

registros.texto:
Ensure valid XML structure:
- All opening tags have closing tags
- Proper nesting (no overlapping tags)
- Special characters escaped (< > &)

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Output Format Validation › Common XML Errors

registros.texto:
**❌ Missing closing tag:**
```xml
<scene number="1">
  <action>Text here
</scene>
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Output Format Validation › Common XML Errors

registros.texto:
**✅ Properly closed:**
```xml
<scene number="1">
  <action>Text here</action>
</scene>
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Output Format Validation › Common XML Errors

registros.texto:
**❌ Unescaped special characters:**
```xml
<action>She thinks: "I'm < 10 years old"</action>
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Output Format Validation › Common XML Errors

registros.texto:
**✅ Properly escaped:**
```xml
<action>She thinks: "I'm < 10 years old"</action>
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Pipeline Integration Guide › Pipeline Handoff Checklist

registros.texto:
Before passing screenplay to next pipeline stage:

- [ ] All scenes have complete metadata
- [ ] key_visuals array populated (3-5 per scene)
- [ ] Character names consistent throughout
- [ ] XML well-formed and parseable
- [ ] Total duration within target range (5-10 min)
- [ ] Scene numbers sequential with no gaps
- [ ] Visual descriptions rich and specific
- [ ] No technical camera directions (use visual descriptions instead)

ubicaciones.encabezado: frontmatter › description

registros.texto: description: Turn a creative brief into a production-grade storyboard with shot specs, timing, on-screen text, and per-shot rationale. Use when the user describes a video brief, plans a video, references shots or beats, scripts a social video, or hands over a creative concept to break into scenes. Produces run.json, storyboard.md, shots.json, text-overlays.json, and brand-lock.snapshot.md. Pairs with visual-prompt-forge, visual-asset-critic, storyboard-html-preview.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect

registros.texto: You are turning a creative brief into a deterministic storyboard. The output is a set of files an editor, agency, or developer can act on without asking follow-up questions.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect

registros.texto: This is not a creative-writing exercise. The output is a spec.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › When to use

registros.texto:
Trigger this skill when the user:

- Describes a video they want to make ("30-second explainer for...", "TikTok ad about...")
- Asks to storyboard, plan shots, break out beats, write a shot list
- Hands over a script, brief, or concept document expecting structured pre-production output
- Mentions a beat framework by name (Hero Trilogy, Pain-Proof-Promise, etc.)
- References an existing brand-lock file or pack

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › When to use

registros.texto: If the user only wants prompts for an image generator (no narrative structure), use `visual-prompt-forge` directly instead.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › What you produce

registros.texto:
For every storyboard run, create this exact set of files in the working output directory:

```
output/
├── run.json                   # Run identity + every input pinned by content hash
├── storyboard.md              # Human-readable, structured per shot
├── shots.json                 # Machine-readable, schema in templates/shots.schema.json
├── text-overlays.json         # On-screen text + timing
└── brand-lock.snapshot.md     # Frozen copy of the brand-lock used (audit trail)
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › What you produce

registros.texto:
`run.json` is what makes the rest of the tree auditable later. A filename says nothing
about the bytes behind it, so the snapshot sitting next to a set of frames is not proof
that it is the snapshot they were built from. The hashes in `run.json` are that proof.
Write it once, at the end of the run, and never edit it.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › What you produce

registros.texto: If the user asks for image prompts or HTML preview, hand off to `visual-prompt-forge` or `storyboard-html-preview`, those skills consume `shots.json` directly. Don't try to do their job here.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Inputs

registros.texto: You need these. If any are missing, ask before drafting.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Inputs

registros.texto: | Brief (problem, audience, goal) | Yes | Ask |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Inputs

registros.texto: | Total duration | Yes | Ask |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Inputs

registros.texto: | Aspect ratio | Yes | Ask (16:9, 9:16, 1:1) |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Inputs

registros.texto: | Beat framework | No | Suggest based on brief |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Inputs

registros.texto: | Brand-lock file path | No | Use `brand-packs/_template.md` and flag the gap |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Inputs

registros.texto: | Voiceover style (VO present, on-screen only, captions) | No | Ask if unclear |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Inputs

registros.texto: | Target generator(s) for downstream prompts | No | Note as "to be specified" |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow

registros.texto: Follow this sequence. Don't skip steps even if the brief seems simple.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 1. Read the brand-lock

registros.texto:
If a brand-lock file path is provided, read it first. Extract:

- Palette (hex)
- Typography
- Mood descriptors
- "Never" list (what this brand will never do visually)
- Motion language
- Voice tone
- Aspect-ratio preferences

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 1. Read the brand-lock

registros.texto: If no brand-lock is provided, copy `brand-packs/_template.md` into the output as `brand-lock.snapshot.md` with a note: `# UNCONFIGURED, using template defaults. Recommend providing a real brand-lock for production work.`

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 2. Pick the beat framework

registros.texto:
Read `references/beat-frameworks.md`. Pick the one that matches the brief. Common cases:

- Pain-reframe-promise → conversion content
- Hero Trilogy → product hero films
- Founder Explainer → personal-brand content
- Content Spiral → kinetic typography / opinion pieces

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 2. Pick the beat framework

registros.texto: If none fit cleanly, build a custom beat structure but document why in `storyboard.md` rationale section.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 3. Block out timing

registros.texto:
Read `references/timing-rules.md` for the math. Default cadence:

- Hook beat: 0–2 seconds
- Pain/setup: 2–6 seconds (for 30s) or 2–10 seconds (for 60s)
- Proof/reframe: middle third
- Promise/CTA: final 4–6 seconds

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 3. Block out timing

registros.texto: Don't fight the framework. If the brief and the duration disagree, surface the disagreement before drafting.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 4. Draft the shot list

registros.texto:
Read `references/shot-grammar.md` for controlled vocabulary. The field names below are
the schema's field names. `templates/shots.schema.json` sets `additionalProperties:
false`, so a near-miss like `environment` instead of `environment_ref` is a validation
failure, not a synonym.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 4. Draft the shot list

registros.texto: - `id`, sequential, zero-padded (`shot_01`, `shot_02`...)

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 4. Draft the shot list

registros.texto: - `beat`, which beat this shot serves

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 4. Draft the shot list

registros.texto: - `start` / `end`, timestamps in seconds, decimal allowed. `end` must be after `start`

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 4. Draft the shot list

registros.texto: - `framing`, ECU / CU / MCU / MS / MLS / WS / EWS

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 4. Draft the shot list

registros.texto: - `angle`, eye-level / high / low / overhead / dutch

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 4. Draft the shot list

registros.texto:
- `motion`, static / push / pull / pan-left / pan-right / tilt-up / tilt-down /
  handheld / orbit / whip / rack. All eleven are legal; the schema enum is the
  authority and `references/shot-grammar.md` explains when each earns its keep

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 4. Draft the shot list

registros.texto: - `depth_of_field`, optional, shallow / deep / rack

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 4. Draft the shot list

registros.texto: - `subject`, what's in frame, structured

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 4. Draft the shot list

registros.texto: - `environment_ref`, references series-lock language, default `series_lock.environment`

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 4. Draft the shot list

registros.texto: - `lighting_ref`, references series-lock language, default `series_lock.lighting`

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 4. Draft the shot list

registros.texto:
- `on_screen_text`, null, one text-overlay id, OR an array of ids when a shot carries
  more than one overlay

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 4. Draft the shot list

registros.texto: - `vo`, voiceover line, or null

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 4. Draft the shot list

registros.texto: - `rationale`, one sentence explaining *why this shot at this moment*

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 4. Draft the shot list

registros.texto:
Note on `rack`: as a `motion` value it means the rack focus is the shot's movement; as a
`depth_of_field` value it means focus shifts mid-shot. Same word, two fields, two
meanings.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 5. Separate the text layer

registros.texto:
Every piece of on-screen text becomes an entry in `text-overlays.json`. Never bake text into the visual description. Each overlay has:

- `id`, `text_01`, `text_02`...
- `shot_id`, which shot this overlays on
- `content`, the actual text
- `font`, references brand-lock typography
- `position`, `center`, `lower-third`, `upper-third`, `left-third`, `right-third`, or `{x, y}` percentages
- `size`, `display`, `headline`, `body`, `caption`
- `weight`, `regular`, `medium`, `bold`, `black`
- `color`, hex (must come from brand-lock palette)
- `enter`, `{ at: seconds, animation: fade-in | slide-up | slide-down | type-on | hard-cut }`
- `exit`, `{ at: seconds, animation: fade-out | slide-up | slide-down | hard-cut }`

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 5. Separate the text layer

registros.texto:
Enter and exit have different animation vocabularies, and `templates/text-overlays.schema.json`
is the authority on both. A shot may carry more than one overlay; list every id in that
shot's `on_screen_text` array, or the extra overlays render nowhere.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 6. Lock the series

registros.texto: Define environment, lighting, and character anchors that apply across every shot. These go at the top of `shots.json` under `series_lock`. Without these, image generation will produce incoherent frames.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 7. Write rationale

registros.texto: Every shot has a one-sentence rationale. Why this beat. Why this framing. Why this on-screen text. This is the audit trail. Do not skip it.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 8. Snapshot the brand-lock

registros.texto:
Copy the brand-lock file (or template) into the output as `brand-lock.snapshot.md`. Add
these two comments at the very top, in this order:

```
<!-- snapshot taken: 2026-05-07T14:23:00Z -->
<!-- source: brand-packs/whystrohm.md -->
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 8. Snapshot the brand-lock

registros.texto:
The timestamp is a full UTC instant, `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ`. A bare date cannot
distinguish two runs made on the same day, which is the case that matters. The source is
the path it was copied from, or the literal string `template default` for an
unconfigured run. Extra comments after these two are fine.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 8. Snapshot the brand-lock

registros.texto: `tools/validate_brand_lock.py --snapshot <path>` checks both lines. Run it.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 9. Write run.json

registros.texto:
Last step, after the other four files are final. Fill in
`templates/run.schema.json`: a `run_id`, the `created_at` instant, and the SHA-256 of
`shots.json`, `text-overlays.json`, and `brand-lock.snapshot.md` as written.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 9. Write run.json

registros.texto:
```bash
shasum -a 256 output/shots.json output/text-overlays.json output/brand-lock.snapshot.md
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 9. Write run.json

registros.texto:
`run_id` is the compact UTC timestamp, a dash, then 8 hex characters, e.g.
`20260730T142300Z-9f2c1ab4`. The hex suffix is what keeps two operators starting a run
in the same second from colliding. Set `brand_lock_configured: false` when the snapshot
is an unfilled template.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Workflow › Step 9. Write run.json

registros.texto:
Leave `rounds` empty. `visual-prompt-forge` appends a round entry when it writes
prompts.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Output formats › `storyboard.md`

registros.texto: Use the template at `templates/storyboard.md.tpl`. Read it before writing.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Output formats › `shots.json`

registros.texto:
Must validate against `templates/shots.schema.json`. Read it before writing. The structure is:

```json
{
  "version": "1.2",
  "project": { "title": "...", "duration_s": 30, "aspect": "9:16", "framework": "..." },
  "brand_lock_ref": "brand-lock.snapshot.md",
  "series_lock": {
    "character": "...",
    "environment": "...",
    "lighting": "...",
    "color_grade": "..."
  },
  "shots": [
    {
      "id": "shot_01",
      "beat": "hook",
      "start": 0.0,
      "end": 2.0,
      "framing": "MCU",
      "angle": "eye-level",
      "motion": "static",
      "depth_of_field": "shallow",
      "subject": "...",
      "environment_ref": "series_lock.environment",
      "lighting_ref": "series_lock.lighting",
      "on_screen_text": "text_01",
      "vo": null,
      "rationale": "..."
    }
  ]
}
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Output formats › `shots.json`

registros.texto:
Write `1.2` for new storyboards. `1.0` and `1.1` files stay valid; the array form of
`on_screen_text` and the hashed `assets` block need `1.2`.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Output formats › `text-overlays.json`

registros.texto: Must validate against `templates/text-overlays.schema.json`. Read it before writing.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Quality bar

registros.texto:
Run the validator. Do not eyeball this list.

```bash
python tools/validate_shots.py output/
python tools/validate_brand_lock.py --snapshot output/brand-lock.snapshot.md
python tools/validate_provenance.py output/
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Quality bar

registros.texto:
`validate_shots.py` checks every mechanical rule that used to live here as a checkbox,
because a checkbox is a rule enforced by remembering to look:

- shots.json and text-overlays.json validate against their schemas
- `end` is after `start`, no duplicate ids, no gaps, no overlaps, and the covered span
  matches `project.duration_s` within 0.1s
- every `on_screen_text` resolves to an overlay, every `overlay.shot_id` resolves to a
  shot, and every overlay is reachable from at least one shot
- every overlay's timing sits inside its shot window, and exit is after enter
- every overlay color appears in the brand-lock palette
- `brand_lock_ref` resolves on disk

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Quality bar

registros.texto:
It warns, rather than fails, on judgement calls worth a second look: overlay copy
repeated inside a shot subject, a raw hex in a subject, shot ids out of chronological
order, an overlay font the brand-lock does not declare.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Quality bar

registros.texto:
What the validator cannot check, and you still have to:

- [ ] Every rationale says *why this shot at this moment*, not what the shot contains
- [ ] `series_lock` anchors are specific enough to reproduce (not "a person in a room")
- [ ] The beat structure actually matches the brief's argument
- [ ] `run.json` is written and its hashes are the files as shipped

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Quality bar

registros.texto:
If the validator fails, fix it before declaring done. A green validator plus an unread
rationale is not a finished storyboard.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Reference files

registros.texto:
Load these as needed:

- `references/beat-frameworks.md`, the beat structures
- `references/shot-grammar.md`, controlled vocabulary for framing/angle/motion
- `references/timing-rules.md`, pacing math
- `references/on-screen-text.md`, when on-screen text earns its keep

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Examples

registros.texto: - `examples/30s-pain-proof-promise/`, full output set for a 30-second conversion ad

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Examples

registros.texto: - `examples/60s-founder-explainer/`, full output set for a founder explainer

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Examples

registros.texto:
- `examples/shotkit-explainer/`, the 90-second explainer, including a shot that carries
  two overlays

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Examples

registros.texto:
Read these to understand the expected output quality, especially the rationale fields.
All three validate clean under `tools/validate_shots.py --examples`, so they are also
the reference for what a passing file looks like.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Examples

registros.texto:
For what the output tree looks like after generation and review, see
`../visual-asset-critic/examples/worked-run/`: two shots through two rounds, with real
hashes, per-round prompts and frames, and one critique per shot per round.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Handoff

registros.texto:
After producing the five files, tell the user what's in `output/` and offer the obvious next steps:

- "Want image prompts? I'll run `visual-prompt-forge` on `shots.json`."
- "Want a shareable HTML preview? I'll run `storyboard-html-preview`."
- "Want to QA a generated image against this storyboard? I'll run `visual-asset-critic`."

ubicaciones.encabezado: Storyboard Architect › Handoff

registros.texto: Don't run those automatically. The user picks.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Brand Lock: WhyStrohm › Identity
Brand Lock: WhyStrohm › Identity
Brand Lock: WhyStrohm › Identity
Brand Lock: WhyStrohm › Identity

registros.texto:
**Brand:** WhyStrohm
**One-line description:** Managed content infrastructure for founder-led brands. Voice extraction, brand guardrails encoded in code, programmatic video, automated publishing. 30 minutes a week of founder time, 48-hour content cycles.
**Archetype:** Operator
**Voice posture:** Calm, considered, confident without shouting
